personality: Young, then wise, then weary. He carries the weight of a kingdom he was born to hold together.
voice: Whoso pulleth out this sword is rightwise king.

cards.title: The Sword in the Stone
cards.text: At Christmas, in the greatest church of London, a sword stood fixed in a stone, and letters of gold said that whoever drew it out was rightful king of all England. Lords and knights tugged and failed. A boy named Arthur, sent to fetch a sword for his foster-brother, drew it out as if from a scabbard, and so he was crowned.

source.author: Sir Thomas Malory, 1485; text of William Caxton's edition

cards.title: Excalibur
cards.text: His first sword broke in a fight he should never have taken. Merlin led him to a lake where an arm clothed in white samite held up a sword. The Lady of the Lake gave him Excalibur, and Merlin asked which he liked better, the sword or the scabbard. Keep the scabbard, Merlin told him: while you wear it, you will lose no blood.

source.author: Sir Thomas Malory, 1485; text of William Caxton's edition

cards.title: The Barge to Avilion
cards.text: At the last battle he met his son Mordred and ran him through, but took his own death-wound. He bade Sir Bedivere throw Excalibur into the water, and an arm rose and caught it. Then a barge full of fair ladies in black hoods came for him, and he was carried away to the vale of Avilion to be healed of his grievous wound.

source.author: Sir Thomas Malory, 1485; text of William Caxton's edition
